name: Aloo Tikki Burger
steps: Boil potatoes until fully tender, drain well and peel. Mash while warm, then cool until no steam remains. Mix in rice flour, cumin, coriander, chaat masala, Kashmiri chili powder and salt; a dry mixture holds a patty better than wet mash.
Divide into four equal portions and shape broad patties slightly wider than the buns. If the mash feels sticky, chill it 10 minutes; do not add lots of extra flour or the tikkis will become dense.
Heat 35 ml oil on a flat pan over medium heat. Cook the tikkis 4–5 minutes per side until the outside is crisp and deep golden and the rice flour is cooked. Turn gently once; keep warm.

Slice eggless buns and toast their cut surfaces in the remaining 10 ml oil. Wash and dry lettuce; slice tomato, cucumber and red onion thinly. Spread coriander-mint chutney on the lower bun and sweet tamarind chutney on the upper bun.
Set one hot aloo tikki on each lower bun. Add lettuce, tomato, cucumber and red onion, close with the upper bun and serve immediately while the tikki is crisp.
tips: The potato tikki is distinct from the bean-and-mushroom veggie burger. The reviewed photo shows a visibly golden potato patty, two chutneys, lettuce, cucumber, tomato and onion in an egg-free sesame bun.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
